note.title: Yellowed note
note.headline: Remember.
note.body: Remember the beginning. Count the lost. Listen to their calls. Do not forget how long we waited.

opening.title: Newspaper 1 · The Opening
opening.headline: Happyland opens to great success!
opening.body:
The new Happyland children's play paradise opened its doors with colourful garlands and a large birthday celebration. Families were already waiting outside by early afternoon.

The party began on 6 June. A total of 13 children had been invited. Places had been set for them in the party hall, with a trip to the ball pit planned afterwards.

The operator described it as a place where children could forget the time. More parties were planned for the coming weeks. A staff member showed the guests around the new crawl tunnels and the little cinema.

At the end of the event, the entrance remained locked for a long time. When asked why, staff said that the group had not yet fully assembled.
opening.footer: The bottom edge has been cut off. The author's name is missing.

missing.title: Newspaper 2 · The Disappearance
missing.headline: Children missing after incident
missing.body:
Emergency services are continuing to search for missing children following an incident at the Happyland play paradise. Accounts of what happened that evening contradict one another.

According to police, 9 children were initially brought out of the building. The others remained missing. The original guest list recorded a total of 13 children.

Relatives waited outside the entrance until the early hours of the morning. A spokesperson would not confirm which parts of the building had already been fully searched.

Management referred to a technical fault. The venue remains closed for the time being. Police are asking witnesses to come forward and warn against entering the building independently.
missing.footer: A question has been pencilled beside the article: Who changed the list?

coverup.title: Newspaper 3 · The Cover-up
coverup.headline: Operator contradicts witnesses
coverup.body:
New statements raise questions about when the incident at Happyland is believed to have taken place. Investigators are examining management's account.

Investigations indicate that two people independently called the emergency services that night. A total of 2 emergency calls were made. Both callers reported children inside the building.

Management denies, however, that children were in the building at that time. A representative said the party hall had long since been cleared.

One witness disagrees: calls could still be heard from the direction of the kitchen. Investigators say they were only granted access to internal records after a delay.
coverup.footer: A broad grease stain covers the final column. The paragraph about the emergency calls is still legible.

closure.title: Newspaper 4 · The Closure
closure.headline: Happyland permanently closed
closure.body:
The Happyland children's play paradise will not reopen. Its windows have been darkened and the play equipment remains inside the building.

After 8 months of investigation, the inquiry was closed without a conclusive result. The whereabouts of the missing children could not be confirmed.

The operators announced that the premises would be sealed. Records would be placed in storage. A planned public statement never took place.

Relatives are still leaving flowers outside the door. One card reads: We have not forgotten. Nor have we forgotten how long we waited.
closure.footer: The paper smells of damp plastic. Someone pushed it deep into the tunnel.

casefile.title: The abandoned case file
casefile.headline: Four places remain empty.
casefile.body:
There are thirteen tally marks on the back of the guest list. Nine have been ticked off. The remaining four have been traced over again and again.

The file contains transcripts of the two emergency calls. The callers' voices were never identified. Both name the play paradise. Both contradict management's later statement.

The records end after eight months. There is no final report confirming what happened to the four children. Only a note: Premises closed. Records remain on site.

An unlabelled sheet lies between the pages. It bears the same sentence as the door: Remember the beginning.

You can leave the room again. Your night shift is not over yet.
casefile.footer: An answer is still missing. Just because nobody kept looking does not mean nobody is still here.

patrol_hint.title: Newspaper · Back at the Beginning
patrol_hint.headline: You are here again.
patrol_hint.body: So you think walking through the same room 13 times will reveal the secret? Take another, closer look during patrols 3, 5, 8 and 11…
